mappings.note: the 1919 Act's shortcomings are the post-war political disappointment that fed into Non-Cooperation, the nearest LO-3 gets; the frame has no outcome for constitutional reform as such
the eleven demands and why salt was the most stirring of them is the construction of the campaign -- LO-2
the repression around the Rowlatt Act is the trigger LO-3 names; the satyagraha answer to it would be LO-2
the two stages Gandhiji proposed -- surrender of titles and boycott, then full civil disobedience -- is the strategy itself, LO-2
the Cripps Mission (1942) is a decade past this chapter; only the Congress's reasons for rejecting it touch the frame, so LO-2 by nearest fit -- record as a poor fit
Champaran, Kheda and Ahmedabad are the local trials of satyagraha and how they were settled -- the textbook LO-2 question
why the towns fell away (khadi costly, no alternative institutions, students returning) is about the urban base, LO-1, not about whether the technique was sound
verbatim repeat of item 78 -- the demands in the Irwin letter and the salt choice, LO-2
the case against the two-nation theory rests on a shared past and common suffering, the making of one people -- LO-1's collective belonging, argued through the reinterpretation of history
asking how the Salt March worked as resistance is LO-2's 'evaluate the effectiveness of the strategies' in so many words
why dalits largely stayed out is the boundary of collective belonging, LO-1; the Poona Pact that followed would be LO-2
the Muslim community's lukewarm response and its causes is a group's distance from the movement, LO-1
the Nagpur adoption and Gandhiji's staged plan is the programme's design, LO-2; the grievances behind it would be LO-3
four ways the war fed the national movement is LO-3's summary of the war's effects
satyagraha explained as a technique of soul force is the method LO-2 covers, independent of any one movement
the Rowlatt Act and the popular reaction to it is the post-war provocation of LO-3
the Khilafat issue from the Ottoman defeat onward, and why Gandhiji took it up, is the alliance LO-3 names as flowing from the war
the Gudem tribals' own definition of swaraj (forests, no begar, no taxes) is LO-1; Raju's mixture of khadi and violence is described, not evaluated as a Gandhian strategy
the halving of cloth imports is what the boycott achieved, i.e. the effectiveness of the strategy (LO-2); who did the boycotting would be LO-1
Baba Ramchandra and the Awadh peasants' grievances is rural participation, LO-1
why the Patidars and Jats joined -- falling crop prices against an unmoved revenue demand -- is one group's reason for joining, LO-1
the poor peasants' distance from the Congress over unremitted rent is the other side of the same LO-1 question about who the movement held
peasants' reasons for joining Civil Disobedience is participation, LO-1; the salt demand appears only as the occasion
the industrial working class's absence, and the Congress's reluctance over their demands, is LO-1's account of which groups the movement reached
Gandhiji's return and the satyagrahas he organised at once is the method being introduced -- LO-2
